phase1.C-EO-L: I want today's plan refreshed because soccer moved, milk is still needed, and the dentist appointment cannot change. I need a simple explanation of what moved so I can continue without rechecking everything.
phase1.C-EO-B: I have two children, one bathroom, one oven, and only ninety minutes to get everyone ready. I want a realistic minute-by-minute plan that shows what can happen together and honestly calls out anything that will not fit.
phase1.C-EO-H: I want to see my whole week in one calm view using the events I already know are real. I need Monday through Sunday organized clearly, with conflicts made obvious so I can solve each one before the week becomes stressful.
phase1.C-SL-L: I am struggling with one dense paragraph from class and want the idea to finally click. I need five simple points that reveal its meaning without pulling me into material I have not studied yet.
phase1.C-SL-B: I want to test whether I truly understand my notes instead of simply rereading the same pages. I need five questions that challenge my recall and stay completely within what I have already learned.
phase1.C-SL-H: I want one focused study page because a test is coming and my lecture notes feel scattered. I need a clear path for review so I know what to revisit first.
phase1.C-FC-L: I want one short family update because Thursday soccer remains on the calendar, snack duty changed, and the peanut allergy must never be overlooked. I need everyone aligned and the safety requirement impossible to miss.
phase1.C-FC-B: My children have overlapping Saturday events, and I will have only one car for part of the day. I want a realistic timetable that shows whether both commitments are possible and clearly tells me if something must change.
phase1.C-FC-H: I want to bring our separate family calendars into one trustworthy weekly picture. I need the real conflicts highlighted, the unknowns reduced to a few essential questions, and no imaginary help assumed.
phase1.C-RS-L: I have prices for a few options and want to see the choice clearly without being distracted by products I never considered. I need a simple three-way comparison that helps me recognize the best value for my needs.
phase1.C-RS-B: I have narrowed my search to one set of headset details and want to make a confident choice. I need one recommendation that connects the features I care about to the experience I will actually have.
phase1.C-RS-H: I am close to buying and want to stop circling the same candidates. I need four finalists, a clear reason to reject the rest, and a shortlist I can act on without reopening the entire market.
phase1.C-WC-L: I have the substance of a message but not yet the right voice. I want it to sound like me, stay concise, and preserve every claim exactly so I can share it without hesitation.
phase1.C-WC-B: I need the same facts to work as an email, a social post, and a short blurb. I want each version to feel natural in its setting while keeping one consistent truth across all three.
phase1.C-WC-H: I need momentum on a larger piece without pretending it is already finished. I want a strong structure and an opening section that establishes the direction, so I can review the voice before continuing.
phase1.C-CP-L: I have a short desk-lamp clip ready to share and want it to feel polished without sounding forced. I want three natural caption directions that let me choose the mood and publish with confidence.
phase1.C-CP-B: I have one strong image and want it to feel at home on both Instagram and YouTube. I need a clear creative direction and platform-ready wording that keeps the same idea consistent wherever I share it.
phase1.C-CP-H: I want to turn a Saturday repair project into a satisfying time-lapse story people will enjoy from beginning to end. I need a focused plan for the moments to capture, the cover image, the caption, and the boundaries that keep the project achievable.
phase1.C-PA-L: I am torn between two personal choices and do not yet have every fact. I want to see how each path could unfold, what each would ask of me, and what I still need to learn before I decide.
phase1.C-PA-B: I want to make a personal decision with confidence and know in advance what would tell me to stop. I need a short decision story that connects my priorities to a clear boundary I can trust later.
phase1.C-PA-H: I have collected meaningful words from people I trust and want to hear the shared signal. I need one thoughtful page that brings those voices together without adding advice or assumptions that were never expressed.
phase1.C-TH-L: I want the error that stopped my hobby project on one line to make sense instead of feeling like a dead end. I need a plain-language explanation that helps me recognize the problem and decide my next move.
phase1.C-TH-B: I have one repetitive job in my hobby project and want a small helper I can use later on my own. I need something simple enough to understand, trust, and adjust without rebuilding my whole setup.
phase1.C-TH-H: I want to find why my project restarts every ten seconds without losing the idea I was building. I need the failure explained and the corrected version shown clearly so I can continue with confidence.
phase1.G-CG-L: I have about 90 minutes tonight and want to spend it playing, not searching. I want three inviting choices from games I already own, with just enough context to help me pick one and begin.
phase1.G-CG-B: I want a relaxing twenty-minute game session before bed without getting pulled into menus, backstory, or a long commitment. I need a simple starting path that gets me into the fun quickly and helps me stop on time.
phase1.G-CG-H: I have one open Saturday afternoon and one game I am excited to play. I want the session shaped into three satisfying chapters with natural breaks, so I can make real progress and still finish the day feeling balanced.
phase1.G-PP-L: I know the roster I care about and want to see where each choice truly stands. I need a tight five-row ranking that helps me decide who deserves my time without sending me into a broader debate or shopping list.
phase1.G-PP-B: I have the current stats for my character and want one focused build I can play tonight. I need a clear setup based on the information I trust, so I can commit to it instead of second-guessing every choice.
phase1.G-PP-H: My main character feels different after the latest changes, and I want to understand the impact on the way I play. I need the important shifts pulled from the notes I have so I can adapt with confidence.
phase1.G-CR-L: I have a 12-second desk-setup clip and want people to stop, watch, and remember it. I need several opening ideas, one strong caption, and a clear visual direction that all feel like the same story.
phase1.G-CR-B: I want a 30-second headset piece to move smoothly from idea to finished post. I need the story beats, key visuals, movement, and platform wording aligned so the final piece feels intentional rather than assembled.
phase1.G-CR-H: I am building a six-episode series around one recurring character and want every episode to feel part of the same world. I need the character, visual rhythm, and story rules protected while I keep final creative control.
phase1.G-RD-L: I want my 2D character to move naturally, jump only from solid ground, and make collecting coins feel satisfying. I need those basics to work together so I can play the scene and immediately feel progress.
phase1.G-RD-B: I want one enemy to feel alert rather than mechanical: patrol its space, notice the player, give chase, and return when the danger passes. I need that behavior to feel predictable enough to play and believable enough to enjoy.
phase1.G-RD-H: My dash breaks the experience by passing through walls and sometimes firing twice. I want to understand why it happens and leave with a replacement that makes every press feel responsive, controlled, and fair.
phase1.B-ED-L: I need to choose between bringing in a contractor and pausing the work. I want three credible paths and one direct recommendation so I can make the call without false certainty or invented assumptions.
phase1.B-ED-B: I am walking into a meeting with fresh results and need the room to understand what changed, why it matters, and what decision I need. I want one crisp page that exposes any missing fact instead of hiding it behind confident language.
phase1.B-ED-H: I must make a go or no-go decision today. I want a decision card that shows what success and stopping look like, sets a 30-day boundary, and keeps the conversation focused on the decision actually in front of me.
phase1.B-PO-L: I want everyone to understand who owns the next step, when it is due, and where the work stands. I need a five-row view built from the commitments already made, so the team can act without another meeting.
phase1.B-PO-B: I want to remove the ownership confusion that keeps one workstream from moving. I need each person's part made explicit so decisions, action, consultation, and awareness no longer blur together.
phase1.B-PO-H: I want the important risks and decisions hidden inside standup notes gathered into one living view. I need risks, actions, issues, and decisions made visible so nothing real is lost and nothing imaginary is added.
phase1.B-EN-L: I want to clear duplicate files from my weekend archive without accidentally losing two different files that happen to share a name. I need a dependable little helper I can use myself so the cleanup feels safe and controlled.
phase1.B-EN-B: I want people to submit a publishing request and always know whether it is waiting, moving, or finished. I need a small, dependable foundation that remembers each request and gives me a clear status whenever I check.
phase1.B-EN-H: I want to stop customers from receiving the same post twice. I need to understand how two workers can claim one job at the same time and leave with a reliable way to ensure every job is handled only once.
phase1.B-AF-L: I want to walk into Monday with a clear explanation of why revenue missed plan by $420k. I need a six-sentence note my manager can understand immediately, followed by three smart questions that help me decide what to examine next.
phase1.B-AF-B: I want my VP to see exactly why Q2 spending finished $180k over plan and whether the pressure is likely to continue. I need a concise one-page story that connects the drivers, explains what the result means, and gives me a practical next step.
phase1.B-AF-H: I need to help leadership choose between a $1.2M vendor platform and building our own solution. I want a decision story that makes the tradeoffs visible, shows what could change the answer, and defines the point at which I should stop or move forward.
phase1.B-RP-L: I have evidence of a product problem and want the team to understand the human need behind it. I need one clear statement of the problem, the evidence that supports it, and the most important question still open.
phase1.B-RP-B: I want to describe one meaningful moment in the customer's journey without turning it into an oversized plan. I need a focused story of the situation, the motivation, and the progress the customer hopes to make.
phase1.B-RP-H: I have completed a test and want the learning preserved accurately. I need the result, evidence, and unanswered questions captured in one place, with every missing detail clearly visible for follow-up.
phase1.B-SM-L: I have three approved truths about an offer and want to turn those truths into a message people can understand quickly. I need a concise blurb that feels persuasive because it is clear, not because it adds unsupported promises.
phase1.B-SM-B: I want three messages to guide a potential customer from awareness to interest without changing the story along the way. I need each touch to feel fresh while remaining faithful to the same approved claims.
phase1.B-SM-H: I want to answer the customer objections scattered through my call notes with relevance rather than a rehearsed sales speech. I need each concern paired with an answer grounded in what was actually discussed.
phase1.B-CS-L: I need to tell a customer that store credit is unavailable after the refund window without making the conversation feel cold. I want a short, respectful reply that stays faithful to the policy and leaves the customer feeling heard.
phase1.B-CS-B: I want to resolve a support case with one clear response that tells the customer what happens next and keeps my internal record accurate. If an important detail is missing, I want that gap made visible so I can confirm it before acting.
phase1.B-CS-H: I want my team to answer the same policy situation consistently while still sounding human. I need four reusable responses for approval, denial, more information, and escalation, each making the next step unmistakably clear.
phase1.B-PLC-L: I want this draft to be easier to read without weakening any named requirement or boundary. I need every gap clearly identified so I can resolve it instead of allowing a polished sentence to create a new commitment.
phase1.B-PLC-B: I need to understand which parts of this contract or policy should remain, which may be removed, and which deserve closer review. I want a clear map that helps me focus attention while staying within the language in front of me.
phase1.B-PLC-H: I need a review that helps the team see the real issues before an approaching release ships. I want a concise memo grounded only in the material provided, so the conversation stays specific and actionable.
